# RAFT_AI_Chatbot
This is a combination version of the RAG and Fine tuning to train AI models efficiently

**RAFT**

**Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning**

End-to-End Implementation Guide

_From Raw Data to a Conversational AI Model_

**What Is RAFT?**

RAFT - Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning - is a training methodology that teaches a language model how to reason over a specific, curated body of knowledge while deliberately ignoring distracting, irrelevant information. Think of it less like programming a database and more like training a specialist: you present the model with real-world documents, ask it meaningful questions, and then teach it to find the right answer even when surrounded by noise.

Unlike standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which retrieves context at inference time and hopes the model figures out the rest, RAFT bakes domain expertise directly into the model's weights. The result is a fine-tuned model that is faster, more accurate, and far more cost-efficient in production - especially when your domain is specialized (think internal operations, incident management, or proprietary processes).

|     | **Why RAFT Matters for Your Organization**<br><br>Your daily reports, incident logs, and resolution notes are a goldmine of institutional knowledge.<br><br>Standard LLMs have never seen your internal data - RAFT changes that.<br><br>A RAFT-trained model answers domain-specific questions with precision, attribution, and confidence.<br><br>Reduces hallucinations by anchoring answers to real, grounded source material. |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

**Pipeline at a Glance**

The RAFT pipeline has two major phases. The first is Data Preparation, which runs on your data platform (Databricks or Azure Synapse). The second is Model Training, which leverages free GPU compute on Kaggle or Google Colab for testing before graduating to a managed cloud environment.

| **Phase 1 - Data Preparation**    | Ingest → Clean → Chunk → Generate Q&A Triplets → Export .jsonl                    |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Phase 2 - Model Training**      | Import dataset → Fine-tune base LLM → Evaluate → Deploy or push to HuggingFace    |
| **Recommended Ingestion Cadence** | Daily (for live operational data) or Weekly (for consolidated reports)            |
| **Primary Tooling**               | Databricks Notebooks, Azure Synapse, NVIDIA API, HuggingFace, Kaggle / Colab      |
| **Output Format**                 | .jsonl dataset file - portable and framework-agnostic                             |
| **Enterprise Upgrade Path**       | Automate data pull, switch to Databricks/Azure for training, build React frontend |

**PHASE 1 Data Preparation**

This phase transforms your raw organizational data into a high-quality, structured dataset that can be used to teach a language model. Each step in this phase is deliberate and sets up the quality of everything that follows. Cutting corners here will directly degrade the model's performance.

| **1** | **Data Ingestion - Bring Your Institutional Knowledge In**<br><br>Collect the documents you want the model to learn from: daily operational reports, incident logs, resolution summaries, runbooks, or any structured records that represent your domain expertise.<br><br>Ingestion frequency matters. For operational data that changes daily (e.g., incident tickets), ingest daily. For consolidated summaries or periodic reports, weekly ingestion strikes the right balance between freshness and processing cost.<br><br>Supported source types include structured CSV/Excel exports, JSON logs, plain text files, PDFs, and Markdown documentation.<br><br>Store raw ingested files in a dedicated landing zone (e.g., an Azure Data Lake container or Databricks DBFS path) before any transformation begins. |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **2** | **Data Cleaning - Quality In, Quality Out**<br><br>Raw data is never clean. Before any model ever sees your data, it must be scrubbed of duplicates, formatting artifacts, incomplete records, and noise that would confuse rather than educate.<br><br>Recommended tools: Databricks notebooks with PySpark for large-scale distributed cleaning, or Azure Synapse Analytics Pipelines for orchestrated ETL workflows with visual dataflows.<br><br>Key cleaning operations: deduplication by document hash, stripping HTML/XML markup, normalizing whitespace and encoding, filtering out records below a minimum word count, and redacting any PII or credentials.<br><br>Document your cleaning rules in the notebook itself - future team members will thank you, and it makes auditing easier when model quality degrades. |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **3** | **Bronze Folder Organization - Structure Enables Speed**<br><br>Store your cleaned data in a Bronze layer folder (following the Medallion architecture pattern). While it is technically possible to dump everything into a single folder, segregating files by type pays dividends in processing speed and maintainability.<br><br>Recommended folder structure: /bronze/reports/, /bronze/incidents/, /bronze/resolutions/, /bronze/runbooks/ - matching the logical categories of your data.<br><br>Segregated folders allow your chunking notebooks to target specific file types with tailored parsing logic. A PDF parser and a JSON parser are very different beasts; mixing them in the same pipeline creates fragile code.<br><br>Apply consistent naming conventions and include metadata (e.g., date, source system, data category) in file names or as companion sidecar files. |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **4** | **Chunking - The Heart of RAFT Data Preparation**<br><br>This is where the RAFT methodology begins in earnest. Use the 'chunks' notebook to divide your cleaned documents into semantically coherent passages (chunks), and automatically generate one or more questions for each chunk.<br><br>Why chunk? Language models have finite context windows. Chunking ensures that each piece of text fed to the model during training is digestible and focused on a single idea or concept.<br><br>Chunk size is a tuning parameter. Start with 256-512 tokens per chunk for operational data. Smaller chunks give more precise retrieval; larger chunks provide more context. Experiment with your data.<br><br>For each chunk, the notebook prompts an LLM (via the NVIDIA API) to generate a realistic question that the chunk content could answer. This is your training signal - invest time in prompt quality here.<br><br>The 'chunks' notebook is Databricks-native by default but is designed to be portable. Adapting it to run on Azure ML, SageMaker, or Google Vertex AI requires changing the storage I/O paths and the Spark session initialization. |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **5** | **Storing Chunks - Organized for the Next Stage**<br><br>Once chunks and their associated questions are generated, write them to dedicated Silver layer folders: /silver/chunks/ and /silver/questions/.<br><br>Use Parquet or JSON Lines (.jsonl) format - both are fast to read and well-supported by downstream processing libraries.<br><br>Maintain a join key (e.g., chunk_id) that links each chunk to its source document and its generated question. You will need this for the dataset preparation step. |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| **6** | **Dataset Preparation - Golden Chunks and Distractors**<br><br>This step is what makes RAFT fundamentally different from a standard fine-tuning approach. Run the 'dataset_prep' notebook to assemble training triplets.<br><br>Golden Chunks (D\*): These are the chunks that genuinely contain the information needed to answer the question. They are your ground truth. The model must learn to identify and cite these.<br><br>Distractors (D^k): These are randomly sampled chunks from other documents - plausible-looking but irrelevant to the question at hand. The model is deliberately exposed to noise so it learns to ignore it.<br><br>The ratio of distractors to golden chunks is configurable. A common starting point is 3-5 distractors per golden chunk. More distractors make the task harder but produce a more robust model.<br><br>This adversarial training design is the key insight of RAFT: a model trained only on correct information becomes brittle in production. A model trained to filter noise becomes resilient. |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **7** | **Answer Generation and Final Dataset Assembly**<br><br>With triplets formed (question + golden chunk + distractors), the 'dataset_prep' notebook calls a large language model to generate a high-quality, grounded answer for each question.<br><br>Default configuration uses the NVIDIA free API to access a GPT-120B class model. This is powerful and sufficient for dataset generation. Important: the free tier is rate-limited to 40 requests per minute - build retry logic with exponential backoff into your notebook.<br><br>The generated answer is expected to cite the golden chunk explicitly, teaching the model through imitation to always ground its responses in source material.<br><br>Once all triplets have answers, the complete dataset is serialized to a .jsonl file (one JSON object per line) and written to /gold/dataset/raft_dataset.jsonl.<br><br>For enterprise deployments, replace the NVIDIA free API with any hosted model endpoint - Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI - by updating the API base URL, authentication headers, and model identifier in the configuration cell. |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **8** | **Dataset Export - Bridging the Gap Between Platforms**<br><br>At this point your dataset is complete and ready for model training. Currently, the dataset must be downloaded manually from your cloud storage to your training environment (Kaggle or Google Colab).<br><br>To download: navigate to your storage location in the Databricks UI or Azure Portal, locate raft_dataset.jsonl, and download it directly.<br><br>Enterprise automation opportunity: implement a pipeline trigger that, upon successful dataset generation, pushes the file to a HuggingFace dataset repository or an S3/Azure Blob path accessible by your training infrastructure. This eliminates the manual step and enables fully automated retraining on schedule. |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

|     | **Rate Limit Advisory - NVIDIA Free API**<br><br>The NVIDIA free API has a hard limit of 40 requests per minute.<br><br>For datasets with thousands of chunks, implement a rate-limiter with a 1.5-second inter-request delay and exponential backoff on 429 errors.<br><br>Consider batching overnight runs to avoid disrupting daytime workflows.<br><br>For production scale, switch to a paid API endpoint to remove this constraint. |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

**PHASE 2 Model Training**

With your dataset in hand, you are ready to fine-tune a language model. This phase takes the carefully constructed triplets from Phase 1 and uses them to update the weights of a base or pre-trained model, teaching it to become a domain expert that reasons over your specific organizational knowledge.

| **9** | **Training Infrastructure - Start Free, Scale When Ready**<br><br>For initial experimentation and validation, use Kaggle Notebooks or Google Colaboratory. Both platforms provide free access to GPU and TPU accelerators that are sufficient for fine-tuning smaller models (7B-13B parameters).<br><br>Upload your raft_dataset.jsonl to the notebook environment. Use the HuggingFace datasets library to load it: from datasets import load_dataset; ds = load_dataset('json', data_files='raft_dataset.jsonl').<br><br>Training duration depends heavily on dataset size, model size, and hardware. Expect anywhere from 2 hours (small model, small dataset, A100 GPU) to 12+ hours (larger configurations). Plan accordingly and do not close your browser session.<br><br>When you are satisfied with model performance on the free platforms, migrate your training pipeline to Databricks MLflow or Azure Machine Learning for managed experiment tracking, model versioning, and scalable compute.<br><br>Key training parameters to tune: learning rate (start at 2e-5), number of epochs (2-3 is often sufficient for fine-tuning), batch size (match to your GPU memory), and LoRA rank if using parameter-efficient fine-tuning. |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **10** | **Inference and Deployment - Your Model Is Ready to Talk**<br><br>Once training completes, you can immediately interact with your fine-tuned model directly within the notebook interface using a simple inference loop. This is the fastest way to validate output quality before investing in a deployment.<br><br>For a lightweight internal tool, expose the model via a FastAPI endpoint running on your cloud VM or container service. A simple POST /ask endpoint accepting a question string is all you need to get started.<br><br>For enterprise-grade deployment: build a React or Next.js frontend application that communicates with a hosted model API. This gives non-technical users a polished chat interface while keeping the model infrastructure separate and scalable.<br><br>Consider pushing your fine-tuned model to HuggingFace Hub (using the push_to_hub() method) to enable versioning, easy loading across environments, and optional public or private sharing with your team. |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

|     | **Enterprise Deployment Recommendation**<br><br>Host the fine-tuned model on Azure ML Managed Online Endpoints or AWS SageMaker Inference for auto-scaling, monitoring, and SLA guarantees.<br><br>Wrap the model with a streaming API so your React frontend can display responses token-by-token - users expect this from modern AI interfaces.<br><br>Implement a feedback loop: log user questions and model responses, flag low-confidence answers, and feed corrections back into the next RAFT training cycle. |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

**Prerequisites & Access Requirements**

Before running any notebook in this pipeline, ensure the following credentials and accesses are provisioned and tested. Missing any one of these will halt the pipeline at the point where it is required.

| **NVIDIA API Key**             | Required for answer generation in dataset_prep. Register at build.nvidia.com and generate an API key from the developer portal. Store securely in a Databricks secret scope or Azure Key Vault - never hardcode in notebooks. |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **HuggingFace Write Token**    | Required to download base/pre-trained model weights and, optionally, to push your fine-tuned model to the Hub. Generate from huggingface.co → Settings → Access Tokens. Select 'write' scope.                                 |
| **Cloud Storage Access**       | Read/write permissions to your Bronze, Silver, and Gold storage paths in ADLS Gen2, Azure Blob, or DBFS. Verify with a test write before running the full pipeline.                                                           |
| **Databricks Cluster**         | A cluster with appropriate runtime (13.x ML LTS or later recommended) and sufficient worker nodes. GPU clusters are not required for data preparation - only for training.                                                    |
| **GPU/TPU Compute (Training)** | Kaggle or Colab accounts with GPU runtime enabled, or a paid cloud instance (Azure NC-series, AWS p3/p4, GCP A100 VMs) for production training.                                                                               |

|     | **Security Best Practice**<br><br>Never embed API keys directly in notebook cells. Use environment variables, Databricks secret scopes, or Azure Key Vault references.<br><br>Rotate the NVIDIA API key and HuggingFace token on a regular schedule (quarterly minimum).<br><br>If pushing models to HuggingFace Hub, use a private repository for models trained on proprietary internal data. |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

**Quick Reference Checklist**

Use this checklist to track progress through the pipeline for each training run:

| **☐ Step 1**   | Raw data collected and landed in ingestion zone                     |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **☐ Step 2**   | Data cleaned via Databricks / Synapse notebook                      |
| **☐ Step 3**   | Cleaned files organized in Bronze folders by type                   |
| **☐ Step 4**   | Chunks notebook run - chunks and questions generated                |
| **☐ Step 5**   | Chunks and questions saved to Silver folders                        |
| **☐ Step 6**   | dataset_prep notebook run - golden chunks and distractors assembled |
| **☐ Step 7**   | Answers generated via NVIDIA API - .jsonl dataset written to Gold   |
| **☐ Step 8**   | Dataset downloaded (or auto-pushed to training environment)         |
| **☐ Step 9**   | Model fine-tuned on Kaggle/Colab or cloud training platform         |
| **☐ Step 10**  | Model tested via notebook inference - quality validated             |
| **☐ Optional** | Fine-tuned model pushed to HuggingFace Hub                          |
| **☐ Optional** | API endpoint deployed and frontend application connected            |

_This document describes a practical, field-tested implementation of the RAFT methodology. The pipeline is designed to be modular - each step can be adapted, extended, or replaced without breaking the others. Start small, validate on a subset of your data, and scale with confidence._
